notable_absence.finding: Unlike the DDL statements in this batch, DELETE's Prerequisites table branches on a second axis in addition to credential type: whether the statement includes a RETURNING clause. This produces two separate privilege facts per credential type (DELETE itself vs. RETURNING/referenced keyspaces) rather than one - the clearest example in this batch of the credential-type model needing more than a flat two-value lookup to represent a single statement's access requirements.

cross_component_finding: Recurrence of the known issue docs-issues/capella-pages-cite-server-versions.json: the Optimizer Hints subsection is headed 'Couchbase Server 8.0' and begins 'You can supply hints to the optimizer within a specially formatted hint comment,' citing a literal server version on a Capella DML statement page - the same anomaly seen in createcollection.json, createfunction.json, cost-based-optimizer.json, and datefun.json in this batch.
